verses.zh: 保罗、西拉、提摩太写信给帖撒罗尼迦在父　神和主耶稣基督里的教会。愿恩惠、平安归与你们！
verses.en: From Paul[NOTE:1] and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians[NOTE:2] in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Grace and peace to you![NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “Paul.” The word “from” is not in the Greek text, but has been supplied to indicate the sender of the letter.
For the location of Thessalonica see JP1-C1; JP2-C1; JP3-C1; JP4-C1.

The majority of witnesses, including several early and significant ones (א A [D] I 33 1175 1241 1505 2464 M bo), have ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυριοῦ Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ (apo theou patros hēmōn kai kuriou Iēsou Christou, “from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ”) at the end of v. 1. The more abrupt reading (“Grace and peace to you”) without this addition is supported by B F G Ψ 0278 629 1739 1881 lat sa. Apart from a desire to omit the redundancy of the mention of God and Christ in this verse, there is no good reason why scribes would have omitted the characteristically Pauline greeting. (Further, if this were the case, why did these same scribes overlook such an opportunity in 2 Thess 1:1-2?) On the other hand, since 1 Thessalonians is one of Paul’s earliest letters, what would become characteristic of his greetings seems to have been still in embryonic form (e.g., he does not yet call his audience “saints” [which will first be used in his address to the Corinthians], nor does he use ἐν (en) plus the dative to refer to the location of the church). Thus, the internal evidence is overwhelming in support of the shorter reading, for scribes would have been strongly motivated to rework this salutation in light of Paul’s style elsewhere. And the external evidence, though not overwhelming, is supportive of this shorter reading, found as it is in some of the best witnesses of the Alexandrian and Western groups.tn Grk “Grace to you and peace.”
verses.commentary:
1:1 "Paul" Saul of Tarsus is first called Paul in Acts 13:9. It is probable that most Jews of
the "diaspora" were given two names at birth, a Hebrew name and a Greek name. If so, then Saul's parents gave him both names but why,
then, does "Paul" suddenly appear in Acts 13? Possibly

- others began to call him by this name (he worked with Gentiles)

- he began to refer to himself by the term "little" or "least"

The Greek name Paulos meant "little." Several theories have been advanced about the origin
of his Greek name:

- the second century tradition that Paul was short, fat, bald, bow-legged, bushy eye-browed,
and had protruding eyes is a possible source of the name, deriving from part of a non-canonical
book from Thessalonica called Paul and Thekla

- passages where Paul calls himself the "the least of the saints" because he persecuted the
Church as in Acts 9:1-2 (cf. 1 Cor. 15:9; Eph. 3:8; 1 Tim. 1:15)

Some have seen this "leastness" as the origin of the self-chosen title. However, in a book
like Galatians, where he emphasized his independence and equality with the Jerusalem Twelve, this is
somewhat unlikely (cf. 2 Cor. 11:5; 12:11; 15:10).

Notice there is no defense of Paul's apostleship in this introduction to the Thessalonian
church. Of all of Paul's churches Thessalonica and Philippi were the most supportive.

▣ "Silvanus" This was his Roman name. He, like Paul, was a Roman citizen (cf. Acts 16:37-38). Luke
always calls him "Silas," which is a shortened form of Silvanus. He was a gifted prophet and a respected member of the
Jerusalem church, like Barnabas (cf. Acts 15:22,27,32; 1 Pet. 5:12). He replaced Barnabas as Paul's companion on the
second and third missionary journeys. He helped Paul start the Thessalonica church (cf. Acts 17:4,10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SILVANUS

▣ "Timothy" He was Paul's convert from Lystra on his first missionary journey. Timothy
became Paul's team member on the second journey (cf. Acts 16:1-3) replacing John Mark.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TIMOTHY

SPECIAL TOPIC: JOHN MARK

▣ "church" Ekklēsia means "called out ones." It originally meant a town assembly in
Greek society (cf. Acts 19:32). The Greek translation of the OT, the Septuagint, uses it to translate
the Hebrew qahal, meaning "congregation" (cf. Exod. 12:6; 16:3; Lev. 4:13; Num. 14:5; 20:6;
Deut. 5:22; 9:10; 10:4; 18:16). The early church considered themselves the Messianic "congregation
of Israel," not a "Plan B."

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

SPECIAL TOPIC: SEPTUAGINT

▣ "the Thessalonians" Acts 17:1-9 describes Paul's encounter with these people. See full notes in
the Introduction to Thessalonians.

▣ "in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ" God and Jesus are combined in a syntactical
way by using one PREPOSITION to identify them both (cf. 1 Thess. 3:11; 2 Thess. 1:2, 12; 2:16).
This is one technique used by the NT authors to theologically assert the Deity of Christ. Another was
to attribute OT titles and functions of YHWH to Jesus of Nazareth.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FATHERHOOD OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHRIST JESUS AS LORD

▣ "the Lord" God revealed His covenant name to Moses in Exod. 3:14-YHWH. The Jews
later became afraid to pronounce this holy name, lest they take it in vain and break one of the Ten
Commandments (cf. Exod. 20:7; Deut. 5:11). Therefore, they substituted another word when they read
the Scriptures, Adon, which meant, "husband, owner, master, lord." This is the source of the
English translation of YHWH: Lord.

Often when the NT authors called Jesus "Lord" (kurios), they were asserting the
Deity of Jesus. This affirmation became the early church's baptismal creedal statement, "Jesus is
Lord" (cf. Rom. 10:9-13; Phil. 2:6-11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: BAPTISM

▣ "Jesus" This Aramaic name means "YHWH saves" (cf. Matt. 1:21), equivalent to the Hebrew name "Joshua."
"Jesus" is derived from the Hebrew word for salvation (hosea) suffixed to the abbreviation of the covenant name
for God (YHWH).

▣ "Christ" This is a translation of the Hebrew term for "Anointed One" (mashiach). This
refers to the special calling and equipping by the Spirit for YHWH's assigned task. It is the Hebrew
term for God's Special, Promised, Coming One, "Messiah" (cf. Luke 2:11,26; 3:15; 4:41; 9:20; 22:67;
23:2,35,39; 24:26,46).

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES OF THE SPECIAL COMING ONE, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

▣ "Grace" Paul changed the secular greeting charein (greetings) to charis
(grace), making it uniquely Christian. Grace always precedes peace.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRACE, MERCY, PEACE IN PAUL

▣ "peace" This reflects the Hebrew greeting shalom. The phrase "grace and peace" was
possibly intended to combine traditional Greek and Hebrew greetings.

The King James Version adds a typical Pauline phrase "from God our Father and the Lord
Jesus Christ" from 2 Thess. 1:1 after "peace." This phrase does not appear in the Greek uncial
manuscripts B, F, or G. It does appear in the ancient uncial manuscripts א
and A. A slightly modified form appears in manuscript D. It may be a scribal gloss from 2 Thess. 1:2.
The UBS4 gives the shorter text without the additional phrase an "A"rating (certain).

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

verses.zh: 我们为你们众人常常感谢　神，祷告的时候提到你们，
verses.en: We thank God always for all of you as we mention you constantly[NOTE:1] in our prayers,
notes: Or “mention you in our prayers because we recall constantly…”
verses.commentary:
1:2 "We" This refers to Paul, Silas and Timothy (the believing Jewish mission team). Paul used
this PLURAL PRONOUN more often in 1 Thessalonians than in any other letter. It is uncertain
how this affected the process of writing the book. Paul often used scribes. Exactly how much freedom in
composition these scribes had is unknown.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SCRIBES

▣ "give thanks to God" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE INDICATIVE indicating
continuous action. A spirit of thanksgiving characterizes the entire letter (cf. 1 Thess. 2:13; 3:9). Paul
had a wonderful relationship with this church as he did with the church at Philippi.

Paul's opening prayers are not only culturally expected in Greek style, but often seem to outline
his theological topics.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THANKSGIVING

▣ "making mention of you" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE PARTICIPLE indicating
a purposeful decision by Paul to continue to pray for the churches he started. The syntactical structure of Paul's prayer can
be seen in the three DEPENDENT CLAUSES:

- making mention (1 Thess. 1:2)

- constantly bearing in mind (1 Thess. 1:3)

- knowing (1 Thess. 1:4)

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

verses.zh: 在　神―我们的父面前，不住地记念你们因信心所做的工夫，因爱心所受的劳苦，因盼望我们主耶稣基督所存的忍耐。
verses.en: because we recall[NOTE:1] in the presence of our God and Father[NOTE:2] your work produced by faith and labor motivated by love and endurance inspired by hope[NOTE:3] in our Lord Jesus Christ.
notes: Grk “making mention…recalling.” The participle ποιούμενοι (poioumenoi) in v. 2 has been translated as temporal, and μνημονεύοντες (mnēmoneuontes) in v. 3 has been translated as causal.
Or the phrase may connect at the end of the verse: “hope…in the presence of our God and Father.”
Grk “knowing.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, the participle εἰδότες (eidotes) has been translated as a finite verb and a new sentence started here in the translation.
verses.commentary:
1:3 "constantly bearing in mind" This is a PRESENT ACTIVE PARTICIPLE. This shows
Paul's intense, abiding concern for these believers. He thought of and thanked God often for these
converts, as he did for all the churches (cf. Rom. 1:9; Eph. 1:16; Phil. 1:3-4; Col. 1:9; 2 Tim. 1:3;
Philemon v. 4).

NASB, NRSV
"your work of faith and labor of love and

steadfastness of hope"

NKJV
"your work of faith and labor of love and patience of hope"

TEV
"how you put your faith into practice, how your love made you

work so hard and how your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ is firm"

NJB
"your faith in action, worked for love and persevered through hope"

REB
"how your faith has shown itself in action, your love in labor,

and your hope of our Lord Jesus Christ in perseverance"

Peshitta
"the work of your faith and the labor of your love

and the patience of your hope"

Each of these three phrases is in a grammatical construction that asserts that the

- work is produced by faith

- the labor is produced by love

- the steadfastness is produced by hope

The focus is on active, faithful believers. Faith is always a response to God's initiating activity.

These characteristics form the basis of Paul's thanksgiving to God. In Eph. 2:8-10, grace
and faith are related to good works. These three terms (faith, hope, and love) are often linked in the NT
(cf. Rom. 5:2-5; 1 Cor. 13:13; Gal. 5:5-6; Col. 1:4-5; 1 Thess. 5:8; Heb. 6:10-12; 10:22-24; 1 Pet. 1:21-22).
The order often differs. "Faith," in this context, does not refer to doctrine (cf. Jude 1:3, 20), but to
personal trust (cf. 1 Thess. 1:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH, BELIEVE, OR TRUST

SPECIAL TOPIC: FAITH (NT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVE (agapē)

▣ "labor" "Labor" is a very intense word—Christianity is active not passive
(cf. 1 Cor. 15:58).

▣ "steadfastness" This is not a passive concept either, but an active, voluntary, steadfast
endurance in the face of trials (cf. Luke 21:19; Rom. 5:3-4). It meant to see a need and then voluntarily
help carry the load as long as needed (cf. 2 Thess. 1:4).

▣ "hope. . .in the presence of our God" This refers to the parousia or Second Coming,
a major theme of this letter (cf. 1 Thess. 1:10; 3:13; 4:13-5:11; 5:32; 2 Thess. 1:7,10). Notice that
each chapter ends discussing this very subject. "Hope" does not have the connotation of a doubtful
"maybe" or "could be" as in English, but rather the expectation of an event with an ambiguous time
element.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SECOND COMING

verses.zh: 被　神所爱的弟兄啊，我知道你们是蒙拣选的；
verses.en: We know,[NOTE:1] brothers and sisters[NOTE:2] loved by God, that he has chosen you,[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “brothers,” but the Greek word may be used for “brothers and sisters” or “fellow Christians” as here (cf. BDAG 18 s.v. ἀδελφός 1, where considerable nonbiblical evidence for the plural ἀδελφοί [adelphoi] meaning “brothers and sisters” is cited).
verses.commentary:
1:4 "knowing" This is the third of three PARTICIPLES which relate to
Paul's prayer in 1 Thess. 1:2.

▣ "brethren" This is obviously the generic sense of "brothers and sisters."

▣ "beloved by God" Literally "divinely loved ones." This PERFECT PASSIVE PARTICIPLE
phrase is theologically linked to their election (cf. Eph. 1:4-5). It emphasizes believers continuing
status as "loved ones." The agent of love is God. The ADJECTIVE "beloved" (agapētos)
is usually used of the Fathers's love for Jesus (cf. Matt. 3:17; 12:18; 17:5; Eph. 1:6). It comes to
be used by Paul for those who trust Him by faith and are now also the beloved by the Father (cf. Rom. 1:7;
Col. 3:12; 2 Thess. 2:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELOVED

NASB
"His choice of you"

NKJV
"your election by God"

NRSV
"that he has chosen you"

TEV
"God. . .has chosen you"

NJB
"that you have been chosen"

Peshitta
"the elected ones"

REB
"we are certain that he has chosen you"

While no VERB appears (just the NOUN PHRASE "the
choice of you"), the agent of the action is God in Christ, which is expressed by the PASSIVE VOICE
in the previous VERB, with God specifically mentioned. This is asserting the theological necessity
of God initiating love and choice.

- Matt. 13:11 ‒ "To you it has been granted to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been granted."

- John 3:27 ‒ "A man can receive nothing unless it has been given him from heaven."

- John 6:44 ‒ "No one can come to Me, unless the Father who sent Me draws him,"

- John 6:65 ‒ "No one can come to Me, unless it has been granted him from the Father."

- John 12:32 ‒ "If I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men to Myself."

Paul knew they were chosen because both Jews and Gentiles responded to the gospel! God's choice
was confirmed by His powerful actions expressed in 1 Thess. 1:5.

Election is a call to holiness (cf. Eph. 1:4) and service (cf. Col. 3:12-14; 2 Pet. 1:2-11), not to a
privilege standing!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 因为我们的福音传到你们那里，不独在乎言语，也在乎权能和圣灵，并充足的信心。正如你们知道，我们在你们那里，为你们的缘故是怎样为人。
verses.en: in that[NOTE:1] our gospel did not come to you merely in words,[NOTE:2] but in power and in the Holy Spirit and with deep conviction (surely you recall the character we displayed when we came among you to help you).[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “just as you know what sort of people we were among you for your sakes.” Verse 5 reflects on the experience of Paul and his fellow preachers; v. 6 begins to describe the Thessalonians’ response.
verses.commentary:
1:5 "for our gospel" The gospel is the new revelation from God in the form of a person (i.e. Messiah) predicted
by Moses (i.e. Gen. 15:1,4) and the prophets (i.e. Isa. 1:10; Jonah 1:1). This phrase is equal to "for the word of the Lord"
in v. 8. Verses 8-9 are some of the main pillars of the gospel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES OF THE SPECIAL COMING ONE

▣

NASB, NKJV
"did not come to you in word only"

NRSV
"came to you not in word only"

TEV
"not with words only"

NJB
"it came to you not only as words"

Peshitta
"our preaching to you was not in words only"

More than just an abstract idea, the gospel changed their lives (cf. Romans 1:16;
James 2:14-26). This must be true of gospel preaching today. Holiness
is the goal (cf. Rom. 8:28-29; 2 Cor. 3:18; 7:1; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:4; 4:13;
1 Thess. 3:13; 4:3,7; 5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15). The gospel is

- a person to welcome

- truths about that person to be believed

- a life emulating that person to be lived!

All three are crucial! Justification must not be separated from sanctification.

▣ "in power and in the Holy Spirit There are three related things that confirmed God's choice:

- gospel came in word

- gospel came in power

- gospel came in Holy Spirit

This refers to (1) what happened to the Thessalonian believers personally or (2) God's supernatural work
through Paul (cf. Rom. 8:15-16). There was powerful confirmation of the truth and spiritual power of
the gospel through Paul's preaching and teaching.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

▣ "with full conviction" This "full assurance" (cf. Col. 2:2; Heb. 6:11; 10:22) could refer to

- Paul's preaching

- the Thessalonians' response to the gospel

▣ "as you know what kind of men we proved to be among you for your sake" Paul is contrasting
the way he and his mission team acted among the Thessalonians from other religious leaders.

- preached to them with boldness amidst persecution (1 Thess. 2:2)

- not from error (1 Thess. 2:3)

- not from impurity (1 Thess. 2:3)

- not by way of deceit (1 Thess. 2:3)

- not pleasing men (1 Thess. 2:4)

- not in flattering speech (1 Thess. 2:5)

- not with a pretext of greed (1 Thess. 2:5)

- did not seek glory from men (1 Thess. 2:6)

- proved to be gentle (1 Thess. 2:7)

- having a fond affection for you (1 Thess. 2:8)

- worked night and day so as not to be a burden (1 Thess. 2:9)

- acted devoutly (1 Thess. 2:10)

- acted uprightly (1 Thess. 2:10)

- acted blamelessly (1 Thess. 2:10)

- exhorting, encouraging, imploring each of you as a father (1 Thess. 2:11)

verses.zh: 并且你们在大难之中，蒙了圣灵所赐的喜乐，领受真道就效法我们，也效法了主；
verses.en: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord when you received[NOTE:1] the message with joy that comes from the Holy Spirit, despite great affliction.
notes: Most mss (א A C D2 F G Ψ 0278 1175 1241 1505 2464 M al) have the plural τύπους (tupous, “examples”) here, while a few significant witnesses have the singular τύπον (tupon, “example”; B D*,c 6 33 81 104 1739 1881 lat). With ὑμᾶς (humas, “you”) immediately preceding, the plural form looks motivated: Scribes would be expected to change the singular to the plural here. Although the external evidence for the singular reading is not overwhelming, the internal evidence for it is compelling.
verses.commentary:
1:6 "You also" This PRONOUN is an emphatic contrast to the "we" of 1 Thess. 1:2-5.

NASB, NRSV
"You also became imitators of us and of the Lord"

NKJV, Peshitta
"And you became followers of us and of the Lord"

TEV
"You imitated us and the Lord"

NJB
"and you were led to become imitators of us, and of the Lord"

REB
"You, in turn, followed the example set by us and by the Lord"

"Imitators" comes into English as "mimic" (cf. the Greek term and concept are found
in 1 Thess. 1:6; 2:14; 2 Thess. 3:7,9; 1 Cor. 4:16; 11:1; Gal. 4:12; Phil. 3:17; 4:9).

Christlikeness is God's goal for every believer (cf. Rom. 8:28-29; 2 Cor. 3:18; 7:1; Gal. 4:19;
Eph. 1:4; 4:13; 1 Thess. 3:13; 4:3,7; 5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15).

The image of God in mankind is restored (cf. Lev. 11:44; 19:2; Matt. 5:48; Eph. 1:4; 5:1) by
the gospel. The intimate fellowship of the Garden of Eden with YHWH is restored (i.e. Gen. 3:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

NASB, NKJV
"having received the word"

NRSV
"you received the word"

TEV
"you received the message"

NJB
"you took to the gospel"

Peshitta
"welcomed the word"

REB
"the welcome you gave the message"

This term has the connotation

- "to receive as a welcomed guest" (cf. Matt. 10: 40-41; 18:5)

- "to receive a message" (cf. 1 Thess. 1:4; 2 Cor. 11:4; James 1:21)

This is an AORIST MIDDLE (deponent)
PARTICIPLE. Humans must respond to God's offer in Christ's finished work by repentance
and faith (cf. Mark 1:15; John 1:12, 3:16; Acts 3:16,19; 20:21; Rom. 10:9-13).

Salvation is

- a message (doctrinal truth)

- a person (existential encounter)

- a life to live (1 Thess. 1:6)

We receive the gospel message and befriend Jesus. We must trust completely in both. This
results in a new life of faithfulness and holiness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RECEIVE

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHAT
DOES IT MEAN TO "RECEIVE," "BELIEVE," "CONFESS/PROFESS," "CALL UPON"?

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FAITH

NASB, Peshitta
"in much tribulation"

NKJV
"in much affliction"

NRSV
"in spite of persecution"

TEV
"even though you suffered much"

NJB
"the great opposition all round you"

REB
"meant grave suffering for you"

This is literally "to press" (cf. John 16:33; Acts 14:22; 2 Thess. 1:4,6). Becoming
a Christian does not guarantee a lack of tension-on the contrary, it is quite the opposite
(cf. Matt. 5:10-12; John 15:18-19; Rom. 8:17; 1 Pet. 3:13-17; 4:12-19). Acts 17 describes some of the
persecution Paul (also note 2 Cor. 4:7-12; 6:3-10; 11:23-28) and this church experienced.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRIBULATION

▣ "with the joy of the Holy Spirit" This joy given by the Spirit is so encompassing and
complete that it is a present and sustaining power of hope and confidence even amid great persecution
and pain. It is a joy unaffected by circumstances (cf. 1 Thess. 5:16; Matt. 5:10-12; Acts 13:52; Rom. 5:2-5;
2 Cor. 6:10; 7:4; Gal. 5:22; Phil. 4:4; 1 Pet. 4:13). Joy, like obedience, is an evidence of a true salvation!
For a good small book on joy, see Hannah Whithall Smith, The Christians Secret of a Happy Life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE NT

verses.zh: 甚至你们作了马其顿和亚该亚所有信主之人的榜样。
verses.en: As a result you became an example[NOTE:1] to all the believers in Macedonia and in Achaia.
notes: Or “the word of the Lord.”sn “The word of the Lord” is a technical expression in OT literature, often referring to a divine prophetic utterance (e.g., Gen 15:1, Isa 1:10, Jonah 1:1). In the NT it occurs 15 times: 3 times as ῥῆμα τοῦ κυρίου (rhēma tou kuriou; Luke 22:61, Acts 11:16, 1 Pet 1:25) and 12 times as λόγος τοῦ κυρίου (logos tou kuriou; here and in Acts 8:25; 13:44, 48, 49; 15:35, 36; 16:32; 19:10, 20; 1 Thess 4:15; 2 Thess 3:1). As in the OT, this phrase focuses on the prophetic nature and divine origin of what has been said. Here the phrase has been translated “the message of the Lord” because of the focus upon the spread of the gospel evident in the passage.
verses.commentary:
1:7 "you became an example to all the believers" In some ways this is hyperbolic, but in others very
literal. The Thessalonian believers' joy and perseverance under testing and trial was a source of great
encouragement to other believers. This is also how the suffering of Job, the prophets (cf. Matt. 5:10,12),
the Messiah, and the Apostles (i.e. 2 Cor. 4:7-15; 6:4-10; 11:23-28) affect future believers. Often believers'
most powerful testimony is during times of trial, pain, and persecution.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO CHRISTIANS SUFFER?

▣ "example" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FORM (tupos)

▣ "in Macedonia and in Achaia" These were Roman provinces. Achaia is located within modern
Greece; Macedonia is a political state independent of Greece, though culturally and economically related. Paul
came to this area by the Spirit's command (cf. Acts 16:6-10).

verses.zh: 因为主的道从你们那里已经传扬出来。你们向　神的信心不但在马其顿和亚该亚，就是在各处也都传开了，所以不用我们说甚么话。
verses.en: For from you the message of the Lord[NOTE:1] has echoed forth not just in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place reports of your faith in God have spread,[NOTE:2] so that we do not need to say anything.
notes: Grk “your faith in God has gone out.”
Grk “they themselves,” referring to people in the places just mentioned.
verses.commentary:
1:8 "has sounded forth" This is literally "trumpeted" or "thundered." It is a PERFECT PASSIVE
INDICATIVE which implies that through their joy amidst trials the gospel "sounded forth and still
sounds." In English we get the word "echo" from this Greek word. Verses 8-10 form one sentence in Greek.

▣ "but also in every place" This is an exaggeration (hyperbole) similar to
1 Thess. 1:2 (cf. Rom. 1:8). The Bible, being an eastern book, often uses figurative language. Be careful
of western literalism. See G. B. Caird, The Language and Imagery of the Bible, pp. 22, 110-117, 121, 133, 181.

SPECIAL TOPIC: EASTERN LITERATURE

NASB
"so that we have no need to say anything"

NKJV
"so that we do not need to say anything"

NRSV
"so that we have no need to speak about it"

TEV
"There is nothing, then, that we need to say"

NJB
"We do not need to tell other people about it"

Peshitta
"so that we need not speak anything about you"

An ambiguous phrase, many translations supply "the faith" from the previous clause. This
does not necessarily mean that they understood everything about Christian doctrine (obviously not about the
Second Coming) or even about suffering. But their lives showed that the gospel truly took root in their hearts and
minds. The Holy Spirit will reveal the basics of the gospel to every receptive heart.

In a sense, this is a fulfillment of the New Covenant of Jer. 31:31-34.

verses.commentary:
1:9-10 These verses are a summary of the gospel (cf. 1 Thess. 4:14; 1 Cor. 15:1-4).

- they turned to God (faith)

- from idols (repentance)

- the resurrection

- deliverance from the judgment

- the hope of a Second Coming

- service/worship of the living and true God

This doctrinal list may have been a necessary faith affirmation at baptism.

The summaries of Apostolic sermons in Acts are often called the kerygma ("proclamation").

Remember, every chapter of 1 Thessalonians ends on an eschatological emphasis.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KERYGMA OF THE EARLY CHURCH

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

1:9 "turned to God from idols" This refers to their repentance from pagan idolatry. The gospel is
both negative and positive—repentance and faith (cf. Mark. 1:15; Acts 3:16, 19; 20:21). There is a
"turning from" as well as a "turning to."

The NASB Study Bible (p. 1748) makes the observation that the three evidences
of the Thessalonian conversion were

- turning to God (faith)

- turning from idols (repentance)

- serving God

- waiting for Christ's return

I would add to this list "joy" of v. 6.

▣ "to serve" Literally this means "as a slave." This is a PRESENT INFINITIVE. They
turned (AORIST) from idols and continued to serve the true, living God (cf. Rom. 6:18). This
portrays God as King and His followers as servants. In one sense, we are slaves, in another, we are children.

▣ "a living and true God" This reflects God's covenantal name and character, YHWH (cf. Exod. 3:14). YHWH is
the ever-living, only-living God. This is the basis of biblical monotheism (cf. Deut. 4:35,39; 6:4; Isa. 45:5,6,18,21-22; 47:8,10;
65:16; Jer. 10:10; John 17:3; 1 John 5:20). For a brief discussion of the relationship of YHWH to "life," see Millard
Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., pp. 297-298.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIFE (zōa)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "to wait for His Son from heaven" This is another PRESENT INFINITIVE. They
continued to serve (cf. 1 Thess. 1:9) God and to wait for Christ's return. Paul continued his emphasis
on the Second Coming as the theological keynote of the letter. Every chapter ends on this subject
(cf. 1 Thess. 1:10; 2:19; 3:13; 4:13-18; 5:23).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOPE

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SECOND COMING

▣ "whom He raised from the dead" This was confirmation of the Father's acceptance of the Son's
substitutionary death (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 1 Corinthians 15; 2 Cor. 5:21).

All three persons of the Trinity were active in Christ's resurrection:

- the Father ‒ Acts 2:24; 3:15; 4:10; 5:30; 10:40; 13:30, 33, 34, 37; 17:31

- the Spirit ‒ Rom. 8:11

- the Son ‒ John 2:19-22; 10:17-18

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

▣ "rescues us" This is a PRESENT MIDDLE (deponent)
PARTICIPLE which emphasizes Jesus' continuous action on our behalf. The victory is
ongoing (cf. Rom. 5:9; 8:31-39; Col. 1:13-14). He continues to intercede for us (cf. 1 John 2:1; Heb. 7:25; 9:24).

Some theologians believe this refers to

- the terrible destruction and slaughter of the Jewish war with Rome (A.D. 66-70), see Josephus'
The Jewish Wars

- a secret rapture of the church in 1 Thess. 4:13-18, which will spare them from an end-time period of tribulation

SPECIAL TOPIC: RAPTURE

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRIBULATION

- judgment scenes such as Matt. 25:31-46; Rev. 20:11-15

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

My current understanding leans toward #1, which is known as Partial Preterism. Some helpful
resources for this position are

- YouTube videos by Steve Gregg, "The Olivet Discourse" and "The Modern State of Israel"

- Kenneth Gentry, Before Jerusalem Fell

- Four Views On the Book of Revelation, several authors, pp. 35-92

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER, II. B. #1.

▣ "wrath to come" For some, Jesus' Second Coming is their great hope, but for others it will
be their eternal loss. The believers will experience the persecution and pressure of Jews and pagans,
but they will never experience the wrath of God (i.e. orgē, cf. 1 Thess. 5:9; two words used in Revelation,
thumos and orgē, reflect the same reality).

The wrath of God is coming (PRESENT MIDDLE [deponent] PARTICIPLE)
on all those who reject Christ (cf. 1 Thess. 2:16; Matt. 25; Rom. 1-2). It is surely true that wrath is an anthropomorphic term, but
so too, is "the love of God" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE DEITY

At the end of each chapter in 1 Thessalonians an allusion to the Second Coming is
prominent (cf. 1 Thess. 1:10; 2:19; 3:13; 4:13-18; 5:23). New Testament writers view time and history
through their worldview of a coming day of judgment and reward. The NT is thoroughly eschatological
(cf. How to Read the Bible For All Its Worth by Fee and Stuart, pp. 131-134).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why did Paul not assert his apostleship in this letter?

- What is significant about verse 1?

- Why are faith, hope and love mentioned together so often in the New Testament?

- How is election linked to the believers' actions?

- Why do Christians suffer? How does the Second Coming address the problem of suffering?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO 1 THESSALONIANS 1-10

- 1 Thessalonians 1:1 is a standard letter form of the first century. Paul made it uniquely Christian
by substituting "grace" for the similar sounding Greek word "greetings" (charis vs. charein).
1 Thessalonians is Paul's shortest introductory greeting. He does not even mention his call by God and
apostleship. He did not need to; this church had a special relationship with him.

- 1 Thessaslonians 1:2-10 forms one long thanksgiving prayer to God for the believers at Thessalonica:

- 1 Thess. 1:2-5 forms one sentence that describes Paul's evangelistic witness.

- 1 Thess. 1:6-9 describes the Thessalonians' response.
